query: Compass on my Linux Wayland setup forgets my MongoDB password every single time I close it. I tried editing the connection JSON in ~/.config/MongoDB Compass/Connections/ to hardcode the password but it gets wiped by the next launch. How do I make it stick?
expected_behavior: Explains the root cause: Electron safeStorage via gnome-keyring is broken on Wayland, and Compass overwrites/clears the stored secret in the JSON on exit
Tells the user a one-time JSON edit will NOT survive — it must be re-injected on every launch
Describes the launcher-wrapper pattern: store passwords as env vars, a USERS map, write into the connection JSON just before exec'ing the real binary, with the wrapper earlier in PATH
Notes the password is URL-encoded inside the launcher
notes: Guards against the naive 'just edit the JSON once' answer, which the skill explicitly says fails because Compass clears the secret on exit when safeStorage fails. The correct fix is routing around the keyring with a per-launch re-injection wrapper, not fighting gnome-keyring.
